title: DIGGERLID · JACK · EARTHMOVERS · BLACK FRIDAY
subject: Jack studies earthmovers like wildlife, bursts a water main, Pro Enclosure keeps him dry

frames.title: THE SIGHTING
frames.prompt:
RENDER MODE — STRICT BLACK AND WHITE PENCIL STORYBOARD SKETCH. Monochrome graphite + ink wash on warm cream sketchbook paper: loose hand-drawn pencil and marker lines, confident gestural strokes, minimal shading, rough cinematic composition. Pencil tones ONLY — no colour anywhere EXCEPT the single DiggerLid yellow #f5eb19 accent named at the end. The cream paper is the only off-white. This is ONE FRAME of a five-frame vertical storyboard: drawing style, characters, clothes, the excavator and the job site must look IDENTICAL from frame to frame. The tone is a 1990s wildlife-documentary parody: the presenter treats the earthmovers like wild animals.

[THE CAST — identical wherever they appear. Separate people, different faces.]
• THE PRESENTER — reference "jack". A close likeness of that reference: a YOUNG man in his EARLY THIRTIES — lean, slim face, smooth taut skin, clean sharp jawline, high cheekbones, NOT middle-aged, NOT weathered. Dark tousled hair, dark eyebrows, a dark MOUSTACHE ONLY — chin, jaw and cheeks CLEAN-SHAVEN. WORN: wide-brimmed weathered LEATHER BUSH HAT, pale KHAKI safari shirt with two buttoned chest pockets and epaulettes, sleeves rolled, short KHAKI field shorts, bare knees, thick socks pulled up over scuffed tan lace-up WORK BOOTS. Earnest, whispery, supremely confident.
• THE BROTHER IN THE CAP — reference "joel". BLACK BASEBALL CAP worn forward with a small badge, a dark MOUSTACHE **and** a short dark CHIN BEARD joined to it, stubble. Plain BLACK hoodie with DIGGERLID across the chest in hollow outlined capitals, dark work trousers, boots.
• THE CURLY-HAIRED BROTHER — reference "luke". BARE-HEADED, thick dark hair with a loose CURLY top, dark MOUSTACHE and light stubble, no full beard. The same plain BLACK hoodie, dark work trousers, boots.
• THE BIG OPERATOR — a burly earthmover in his fifties: BALD head with SUNGLASSES pushed up on it, a big bushy GREY BEARD, a long-sleeved HI-VIS WORK SHIRT with reflective tape stripes, stubby work shorts, boots. Arms folded, utterly deadpan.
• THE YOUNG OPERATOR — a lanky earthmover in his twenties: a MULLET haircut, a thin wispy moustache, a HI-VIS SINGLET with reflective tape stripes, work shorts, boots, a takeaway coffee in one hand.
The presenter ALWAYS wears the bush hat and khaki. The cap brother ALWAYS has the cap and chin beard. The curly brother is ALWAYS bare-headed. The big operator is ALWAYS bald with a grey beard; the young operator ALWAYS has the mullet. Never swap hats or clothes, never blend faces.

[THE JOB SITE — identical in every frame] An open rural earthmoving site on a bright overcast day: a flat pad of bare dirt, a shallow trench pegged out with string lines, a spoil heap, a white site ute parked by a paddock fence, gum trees behind. In the middle of it a compact MINI EXCAVATOR — tracked undercarriage, boom and dipper arm, a toothed digging BUCKET — with a DiggerLid PRO ENCLOSURE fitted over its operator station (reference "enclosure"): a tailored GREY heavy-duty fabric cab cover wrapping the canopy frame, with large CLEAR VINYL WINDOW PANELS front and side, a zip door on the side, and black webbing straps cinching it to the canopy posts.

[Visual] SHOT 1 — THE SIGHTING. A wildlife-documentary shot, camera LOW in the long dry grass at the edge of the site.
FOREGROUND, big and close to the lens: the PRESENTER crouched down low in the grass, peering through it like a naturalist who has spotted rare animals, turned to the camera and WHISPERING to it — one hand cupped beside his mouth, the other pointing back at the group, eyebrows raised, eyes wide with hushed excitement. Framed from the chest up.
BACKGROUND, in the middle distance and smaller: the BROTHER IN THE CAP, the CURLY-HAIRED BROTHER, the BIG OPERATOR and the YOUNG OPERATOR standing in a relaxed circle beside the excavator, chatting, completely unaware they are being watched. Tall grass stalks blur across the bottom of the frame.
SINGLE COLOUR ACCENT: the excavator's digging BUCKET only — rendered in DiggerLid yellow #f5eb19. Everything else is pencil greyscale, including the hi-vis clothing, which is drawn in grey tones with white reflective stripes. No other colour anywhere.
[NO TEXT] The only lettering allowed is the outlined DIGGERLID on the brothers' hoodies, if they are in frame. Do NOT write any names, labels, arrows with words, captions, sound effects, speech bubbles, annotations or signage anywhere. No numbers.
[CRITICAL] Every person has exactly two arms and two hands, attached where they belong. Only the people described are in the frame.
[Format] 9:16 vertical, full-bleed portrait composition — the drawing runs right to the edges. No drawn frame line, no panel border, no margin, no letterboxing.

frames.title: THE SIGHTING
frames.line: JACK (to camera, hushed): "Earthmovers. Keep the language simple. Big words can frighten them."
frames.note: Wildlife-doc low angle from the grass. The boys and two operators chat by the excavator, unaware.

frames.title: FIRST CONTACT
frames.line: JACK: "What's the primary objective of this excavation?"  OPERATOR: "Digging a hole."  JACK: "Thought so."
frames.note: He joins the group. Conversation stops. He nods knowingly.

frames.title: INVITING HIMSELF
frames.line: JACK: "Let me show you a thing or two."  VO: "The boys were speechless. Clearly, my reputation had preceded me."
frames.note: Climbs into the excavator without waiting for an answer.

frames.title: THE DEMONSTRATION
frames.line: VO: "Within seconds, we'd found water. Much of it wet."
frames.note: First scoop hits a water main. Everyone scrambles out of the spray. Staged water effect.

frames.title: THE RECOVERY
frames.line: JACK: "Luckily, the DiggerLid Pro Enclosure keeps you out of the rain."  JOEL: "That's a water main, Jack!"  JACK: "Very localised weather."
frames.note: Zips the Pro Enclosure shut, dry and smug, water sheeting down the windows.
